name: Question 1
problem: Find the inverse of the orthogonal matrix $D=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{4}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Therefore, since $D$ is orthogonal, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{-1} & ={D}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} & -\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find the inverse of the orthogonal matrix D=[3545−4535].

a
D is not invertible
b
[5−555]
c
[3545−4535]
d
[35−454535]
e
[3−443]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Therefore, since D is orthogonal, we have

D−1=DT=[35−454535].
